lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Personal Planning Systems Under Real Load
lessonRef.title: Mastery check: recovery after a missed plan

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic recovery after a missed plan task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner is given a fixed scenario on this task sheet: a two-week research project was due yesterday, but the learner (in the scenario) only has the topic chosen and a rough outline, having lost track of the middle steps after a busy week of practices and a family trip.
safetyNotes: This is a scenario-based judgment task about a provided fictional situation; the learner may reference a real experience of their own if relevant, but is never required to disclose one.

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l05-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l05-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l05-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l05-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Name one specific change to how the original plan was built (not 'try harder' or 'be more responsible') that would have caught this breakdown before the deadline, and explain exactly how that change would have surfaced the problem earlier.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u01-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Realism and completeness of the recovery plan: The remaining-steps list covers all necessary work from the scenario's starting point, and the day-by-day timeline is realistic given what is described as already done. | Root-cause identification and prevention: The named change is a specific planning mechanism (such as a mid-project check-in date) that plausibly would have surfaced the missed middle steps earlier. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner apply the same recovery-planning process to a second scenario with a different cause of breakdown (for example, a group project where a teammate did not finish their part), and compare what changes and what stays the same in the recovery approach.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic recovery after a missed plan task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.elapsedWindow: Up to seven days; use only the check-ins explicitly named in the task
duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: paper or a document
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

content: Starting condition: The learner is given a fixed scenario on this task sheet: a two-week research project was due yesterday, but the learner (in the scenario) only has the topic chosen and a rough outline, having lost track of the middle steps after a busy week of practices and a family trip.

resources.title: recovery after a missed plan action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for recovery after a missed plan.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: recovery after a missed plan coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner is given a fixed scenario on this task sheet: a two-week research project was due yesterday, but the learner (in the scenario) only has the topic chosen and a rough outline, having lost track of the middle steps after a busy week of practices and a family trip.
Coach direction: Read the scenario: a two-week research project was due yesterday.
Learner prompt: Identify the specific point in the original plan where things most likely broke down, based on what the scenario tells you was and wasn't finished.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: recovery after a missed plan complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: List the concrete work that still remains to finish the project, in the order it needs to happen starting today.
Response 1 (t2-p1): List every remaining concrete step needed to finish the project from where it stands (topic and rough outline only) to a submittable final draft.
Response 2 (t2-p2): My list includes finding and reading sources, drafting the remaining sections, and a revision pass, not just 'finish the project.'
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: recovery after a missed plan minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.

Reflection: Name one specific change to how the original plan was built (not 'try harder' or 'be more responsible') that would have caught this breakdown before the deadline, and explain exactly how that change would have surfaced the problem earlier.

Success checks: Realism and completeness of the recovery plan: The remaining-steps list covers all necessary work from the scenario's starting point, and the day-by-day timeline is realistic given what is described as already done. | Root-cause identification and prevention: The named change is a specific planning mechanism (such as a mid-project check-in date) that plausibly would have surfaced the missed middle steps earlier.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: recovery after a missed plan supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l05-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g9-u01-l05-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional recovery after a missed plan condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Realism and completeness of the recovery plan: The remaining-steps list covers all necessary work from the scenario's starting point, and the day-by-day timeline is realistic given what is described as already done. | Root-cause identification and prevention: The named change is a specific planning mechanism (such as a mid-project check-in date) that plausibly would have surfaced the missed middle steps earlier..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l05-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

simulationRoute.title: recovery after a missed plan — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the recovery after a missed plan task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Name one specific change to how the original plan was built (not 'try harder' or 'be more responsible') that would have caught this breakdown before the deadline, and explain exactly how that change would have surfaced the problem earlier.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u01-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Realism and completeness of the recovery plan: The remaining-steps list covers all necessary work from the scenario's starting point, and the day-by-day timeline is realistic given what is described as already done. | Root-cause identification and prevention: The named change is a specific planning mechanism (such as a mid-project check-in date) that plausibly would have surfaced the missed middle steps earlier.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u01-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
